subject: Vocabulary
description: Common antonym pairs from SSC and banking exams

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'ABUNDANT'.
questions.explanation: Abundant = very plentiful. Its opposite is scanty / scarce / meagre. 'Plenty', 'ample', 'profuse' are all synonyms of abundant (common trap — 3 synonyms vs 1 antonym). Related families — ABUNDANCE vs SCARCITY; PLENTIFUL vs DEFICIENT.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'FRUGAL'.
questions.explanation: Frugal = careful with money; sparing. Opposite = extravagant / lavish / wasteful / prodigal. 'Thrifty', 'economical', 'prudent' are synonyms. Note: a 'prodigal son' returns after having been extravagant — 'prodigal' itself means wasteful, NOT 'returning'.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'AMATEUR'.
questions.explanation: Amateur = one who does something for love, not for payment or profession. Opposite = professional / expert / virtuoso. 'Novice', 'beginner', 'layman' all overlap with amateur. Rule: 'amateur' comes from Latin 'amare' (to love).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'BENEVOLENT'.
questions.explanation: Benevolent = wishing to do good; kindly. 'Bene' = good, 'male' = bad, 'volens' = wishing. Its direct opposite is malevolent = wishing evil. 'Kind', 'generous', 'charitable' are synonyms. Same root pair — 'benediction' (blessing) vs 'malediction' (curse).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'TRANSPARENT'.
questions.explanation: Transparent = light passes through; you can see clearly. Opposite = opaque = light does not pass through at all. 'Translucent' lets some light through but is not fully see-through (frosted glass) — NOT the direct opposite. 'Visible' describes what can be seen, unrelated to 'through-ness'.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'OBSOLETE'.
questions.explanation: Obsolete = no longer in use; out of date. Opposite = modern / current / contemporary / up-to-date. 'Antique', 'outdated', 'archaic' are all synonyms of obsolete (again, three synonyms vs one antonym — a classic 3+1 pattern).
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to 'CONCEAL'.
questions.explanation: Conceal = to hide. Opposite = reveal / expose / disclose / unveil. 'Hide', 'disguise', 'bury' are all near-synonyms. Related families — CONCEAL vs DISCLOSE; COVER vs UNCOVER; COVERT vs OVERT.
